title: Banjo tuned like a ukulele; piano from a cousin
summary: Mr. Collins' band needed a banjo player, so he tuned it like a ukulele and played chords; a cousin showed him a piano piece.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, what about, who else inspired you on the banjo and ukulele and all those instruments?

Well, Mr. Collins, the trombone player in this band I was telling you about this while ago. I didn't want to play, but a fellow, the fellow with the head played with him died, a young fellow, he died. So, he needed a banjo player and I couldn't, didn't even know how to tune the banjo to tell the truth. I was playing, I tuned it in ukulele style and played my chords from that.
Same thing as Danny Barker, he told me that same thing, a lot of guys did that. That's what I did.

But Danny Banger also, they all started like that. I tuned it in ukulele and played that night and I made, I made good that night, so I stayed with the band. Before the banjo or after the... No, that was before the banjo. I just, I had, let me see, my cousin, James Backnitude, he showed me one piece, My Country Tisley, on the piano and from then on I just picked up the piano. What's the first tune you learned on any instrument? I'm telling you, My Country Tisley was... No, but I mean on anything, not just piano.
